Microscopically, the nodule was hypocellular and consisted of interlacing thick collagen fibres and rare elastic fibres (Fig. 4). A segmental biopsy of the metacarpal bone of the right thumb showed a nodular thickening of the cortical bone. Histology revealed in the nodular thickening of the cortical bone a remodelling with formation of network of thick bone trabecules and formation of numerous enlarged Havers’s channels with fibrotic tissue (Fig. 5). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: BOS article with caption reticular lesions since birth and in-text biopsy elastoma, corresponding to connective tissue nevus / elastoma plaque manifestation. Overview panel shows left leg in context of genu valgum case. B: Close-up of medial knee/leg showing reticular elastoma lesions described in caption and confirmed by biopsy in BOS case. C: Additional view of left lower leg/foot showing same permanent reticular elastoma lesions in BOS case.
panels.attribution_text: Aydın Şimşek et al. Buschke-Ollendorff Syndrome: A Rare Cause of Unilateral Genu Valgum.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.38074. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Reticular skin lesions on the medial surface of the left lower extremity.
in_text_mentions: In further physical examination, the patient had flexion contracture in the left knee, and skin lesions were observed with a reticular pattern over the medial part of the left lower extremity (Figure 2). It was learned that these lesions had developed since birth and were permanent. The patient was referred to the dermatology department, and the pathology result of the skin biopsy supported the diagnosis of elastoma.
